title: New Postal Products
summary:
A new Federal Register notice centers on the Postal Regulatory Commission’s review of several new and updated custom shipping contracts from the United States Postal Service, with an invitation for public comments by October 29, 2025. It also includes a brief update from the United States Patent and Trademark Office on expected paperwork costs and a routine announcement from the Department of Veterans Affairs about senior executive performance review board members.

Who stands to benefit? Large shippers and e-commerce businesses could gain from more tailored postal rates and service options, which may improve delivery speed, pricing, and reliability. The United States Postal Service could strengthen its competitive offerings by refining contract terms and introducing standardized fulfillment products that have been pre-reviewed for quicker approval. The public benefits from the chance to comment on some of these proposals, adding transparency and oversight. The patent office’s cost update gives inventors, startups, and companies better visibility into expected out-of-pocket expenses. The Veterans Affairs announcement supports continued accountability and performance management for senior leaders serving veterans.

Who might be negatively affected? Smaller mailers who are not part of custom deals may worry about an uneven playing field if larger players gain more favorable terms. Some of the postal requests will be reviewed in a streamlined process that does not include public comments or a public representative, which could raise transparency concerns for some observers. On the patent office item, the estimated annual non-labor costs—about $336,973 in total—reflect real expenses that filers must absorb, which can be more burdensome for smaller entities with tight budgets.

If you have a stake in shipping, e-commerce, or mailing, now is a good time to review the details and submit feedback to the Postal Regulatory Commission by October 29 via its website. For those affected by patent and trademark filings, plan for the noted cost burden. And for those following veterans’ services, the Veterans Affairs update signals ongoing attention to leadership performance and governance.
